options.html: Its impossible to conduct
media consumption and suicide.
truly causal research on

questions.solution: A) It’s should be used instead of Its because "Its" is a possessive pronoun, used when something belongs to or is associated with something that has already been mentioned. "It's", on the other hand, is a contraction of "it is" or "it has". In this sentence, we are not indicating possession, but rather making a statement (it is impossible), so "It's" is the correct form to use.

questions.question: Q. 9 Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. What is the price of this fancy dress pink?
questions.questionHtml:
Q. 9 Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

What is the price of this fancy dress pink?
questions.solution: A) The error in the sentence is in the arrangement of the words. The correct sentence should be: "What is the price of this pink fancy dress?" The adjective (pink) should come before the noun (fancy dress) it is describing. In English, adjectives usually precede the noun they modify.

questions.question: Q. 18 Fill in the blank with the most suitable word . The humour of the gods is cruel; or ______ they see more than we do
questions.questionHtml:
Q. 18 Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.

The humour of the gods is cruel; or ______ they see more than we do
questions.solution: • 'perhaps' should be used because the sentence implies the possibility that the gods might know more than humans. Here, in "The humour of the gods is cruel; or ______ they see more than we do", the word 'perhaps' expresses the possibility that it might be true that the gods know more, which fits better than the other options ('unlikely', 'odds', 'however'). Thus, "perhaps" would be the most appropriate choice.
